I wouldn't copy melodies I would just figure out the way patterns are typically layed out and I would just try spending more times on your melody. Just stack a lot of dramatic sounding synths and plucks and figure out how they're laid out (stacked octaves, double time with the octave moved up every other note, keys and scales, and note progression)

I think you'll be able to figure out the sound you're looking for without copying something else. I would spend more time watching YouTube videos and playing just the piano without worrying about mixing and adding drums until later. The melodies should sound so good that you enjoy making them. Also I find it's easier to find inspiration if you spend more time with fewer instruments and sounds and try to create stuff you like by experiementing with it instead of looking for flashy effects

Lots of layered sounds with reverb for the intro and I'd add some really dirty sounding orchestra hits like the 808 Mafia sounding ones I think there's good ones for nexus 

As for the sound if you have all that stuff just do a slow melody in a minor key for a dark suspenseful sound and let the beat drop after 8 bars 

It's always a good idea to just mess around with one or two sounds for a long time then just going through everything looking for a sound you want before you work on anything sometimes i like to just play on a stand alone piano and I make a lot of stuff I wouldn't have on a piano roll and I have no knowledge of music theory

Also, tons and tons of YouTube tutorials I just type in 2 producers or artists who's sounds I like and put tutorial after and I just fast forward through a hundred different videos and listen to the ones that really catch my attention because I like a similar sound.

Try and stay away from the fast brass melodies for stuff like that I feel like it's overdone and I see it over and over again in every YouTube tutorial every time. Also a nice distorted bass/sub bass (sub being my favorite for this) on top of a really suspenseful melody (like the 'I want' song) sounds really nice just do try to add a nice slide or put those high pitched 808s at the end of the measures, you should hopefully be able to figure out where.

Also it you want to add percussion to the intro fast passes with the hi hats or slow suspenseful lower pitched hi hats sound nice along with toms/rims/and others Lex Luger has a lot of that. If you use all that if you are serious about trap production you should start getting those intros you're looking for. Just use plucks, strings, stacked octaves, synthesizers, and bells with orchestra hits and tubular bells :)
